bug_semantics: OliveTin registered dashboard stream subscribers in a shared client collection and sent every action's execution-start, execution-finish, and output payloads to every subscriber. The subscriber's identity was retained but never checked against that action's log ACL before delivery, so a low-privilege authenticated dashboard user could receive protected action metadata, tracking IDs, usernames, live chunks, and final command output. Ordinary log APIs did enforce per-action authorization.
flaw_origin: Commit e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 first made execution output a global live broadcast: it created internal/websocket/websocket.go, registered every websocket connection in clients, and made OnExecutionFinished serialize the complete LogEntry (including Stdout and Stderr) and call broadcast, which iterated all clients without an action/user authorization decision. Its parent had action-view ACL enforcement but only a passive websocket stub and no execution-output broadcast. Commit db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b later added the explicit Logs permission and filtered GetLogs while leaving the broadcast unfiltered; ac0f3ab6f8346157b1b2a47737ef237e0ae3af8f added globally broadcast live output chunks. The 3k API port a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 carried the existing flaw into Connect EventStream rather than originating it.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3` shows author and committer `jamesread <contact@jread.com>` and the complete message `feature: websocket implemenation at last!`, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: In the validated full-history clone, `git log d4fe9eaa793f508f44bc60f0a1109cb008a6a5b0 -L '/^func (WebsocketExecutionListener) OnExecutionFinished/,/^}/':service/internal/websocket/websocket.go` traces the all-client final-output sink through the path move to e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3; `git log --all --reverse -S'broadcast("ExecutionFinished", le)' --pickaxe-all -- internal/websocket/websocket.go` independently returns e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 as the first writer. `git show e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 -- internal/websocket/websocket.go internal/executor/executor.go` shows OnExecutionFinished constructing a LogEntry with Stdout/Stderr and broadcast iterating every client. Direct parent verification with `git show 6116e954ba5de9936463dbaf76f2e14aef6d9e72:internal/httpservers/websocket.go` shows only accept/read/close behavior, while `git grep -n 'IsAllowedView' 6116e954ba5de9936463dbaf76f2e14aef6d9e72 -- internal` confirms action authorization already existed; therefore the vulnerable output sink is absent in the immediate parent. `git show db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b` shows IsAllowedLogs and GetLogs filtering added without changing websocket broadcast, and `git show --find-renames=40% a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 -- service/internal/api/api.go service/internal/grpcapi/grpcApi.go` shows the later 3k port storing AuthenticatedUser on each stream client yet broadcasting events to all clients. `git log -L '/^func (api \*oliveTinAPI) OnExecutionFinished/,/^}/':service/internal/api/api.go` traces that EventStream sink back to a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 and forward to the fix. `git show acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc -- service/internal/api/api.go service/internal/api/api_test.go` shows the direct fix: mayViewExecutionEvent delegates to the existing log ACL and all three execution event paths now reject unauthorized recipients, with a regression test for a low user versus an admin. Release ancestry gives 2023.10.09 as the first tag containing the original BIC and 3000.0.0 as the first 3k EventStream release. `git tag --contains acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc --sort=version:refname` begins at 3000.11.3; `git grep` shows 3000.11.2 still has the unconditional per-client LogEntry send and no mayViewExecutionEvent, while 3000.11.3 contains the guard. The bundle advisory metadata says `< 3000.10.2` and first patched 3000.10.2, but its own PoC says 3000.10.2 is vulnerable; Git tag contents resolve the actual closing boundary as last vulnerable 3000.11.2, first fixed 3000.11.3. `git cat-file -p e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3` supplies the BIC-only attribution check quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The earliest causal sink is not the large 3k port: the same complete-output fan-out had existed since e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3, survived the later explicit log-ACL boundary and live-chunk addition, and was transported into EventStream by a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404. The immediate parent of e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 lacks any execution-output broadcast, so parent absence is directly established. acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc is both the direct code fix and the fix commit because it adds per-recipient log authorization to execution-start, execution-finish, and output-chunk delivery; the first containing release is 3000.11.3. The BIC is an ordinary single-parent commit, not a squash aggregate, and its raw commit object contains only a human author/committer and no canonical AI attribution. Under the required BIC-only rule, the result is NOT_AI regardless of any later repository AI usage.
